tests.name: Conduct Search Engine Discovery Reconnaissance for Information Leakage
tests.description: Use search engines to discover sensitive information about the target that has been indexed, including exposed documents, configuration files, and credentials.
test_steps: Search for site:target.com in Google, Bing, and DuckDuckGo
Check Google cache and cached versions of discovered pages
Search for sensitive file types (filetype:pdf, filetype:xls, filetype:doc, filetype:sql)
Check robots.txt and sitemap.xml for hidden paths
Search for exposed credentials or configuration files using Google dorks
Review Shodan and Censys for indexed services

tests.name: Fingerprint Web Server
tests.description: Determine the type and version of the web server software running on the target to identify known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations specific to that server.
test_steps: Send HTTP requests and analyze Server response headers
Analyze HTTP response header ordering and default error pages
Use automated fingerprinting tools to identify server version
Send malformed requests to trigger revealing error messages
Compare responses against known server signature databases

tests.name: Review Webserver Metafiles for Information Leakage
tests.description: Analyze webserver metafiles such as robots.txt, sitemap.xml, and security.txt to discover hidden directories, sensitive paths, and application structure.
test_steps: Retrieve and analyze robots.txt for disallowed paths
Retrieve and parse sitemap.xml for complete URL listing
Check for .well-known/security.txt and humans.txt
Look for META tags in HTML source that reveal application info
Check for crossdomain.xml and clientaccesspolicy.xml

tests.name: Enumerate Applications on Webserver
tests.description: Discover all web applications hosted on the target web server, including those on non-standard ports, virtual hosts, and hidden paths.
test_steps: Scan for web applications on different ports using port scanning
Enumerate virtual hosts using DNS brute-forcing and reverse DNS lookups
Discover applications on non-obvious URL paths via directory brute-forcing
Check for applications running on subdomains
Identify different web applications sharing the same server via IP-based enumeration

tests.name: Review Webpage Content for Information Leakage
tests.description: Analyze webpage source code and content for comments, metadata, and other information that may reveal sensitive details about the application.
test_steps: Review HTML source code for developer comments revealing logic or credentials
Check for version information in JavaScript files and libraries
Analyze META tags for framework and CMS information
Search for hardcoded API keys, tokens, or credentials in client-side code
Review JavaScript source maps for original source code exposure

tests.name: Identify Application Entry Points
tests.description: Identify all entry points of the application including forms, APIs, file uploads, and any other input mechanisms that accept user data.
test_steps: Crawl the application to map all pages and forms
Identify all HTTP methods accepted by each endpoint
Map all parameters (GET, POST, headers, cookies) for each entry point
Identify file upload functionalities and their accepted types
Document API endpoints and their input parameters
Identify WebSocket and other non-HTTP entry points

tests.name: Map Execution Paths Through Application
tests.description: Map the execution paths through the application to understand the application's workflow, business logic, and data flow between components.
test_steps: Crawl the application and map all navigational paths
Identify multi-step processes and their required sequences
Map authentication and authorization decision points
Document data flow between client and server components
Identify conditional paths based on user roles or input

tests.name: Fingerprint Web Application Framework
tests.description: Identify the web application framework and its version to discover known vulnerabilities and default configurations specific to that framework.
test_steps: Analyze HTTP response headers for framework-specific headers (X-Powered-By, X-AspNet-Version)
Check for framework-specific cookies and cookie naming conventions
Identify default files and directory structures specific to frameworks
Analyze HTML source for framework-specific patterns and tags
Use automated fingerprinting tools to identify framework and version

tests.name: Fingerprint Web Application
tests.description: Identify the specific web application (CMS, e-commerce platform, wiki, etc.) running on the target to determine known vulnerabilities and attack vectors.
test_steps: Check for application-specific default pages and admin panels
Analyze HTML source for application-specific markers and comments
Identify application by its CSS, JavaScript, and image file paths
Check for application-specific files (wp-login.php, administrator/index.php)
Use automated CMS detection tools to identify the application

tests.name: Map Application Architecture
tests.description: Understand the overall architecture of the application including network topology, server infrastructure, load balancers, firewalls, and backend components.
test_steps: Identify load balancers and reverse proxies via response header analysis
Detect WAF presence using WAF detection tools
Map network infrastructure using traceroute and DNS analysis
Identify backend databases and application servers from error messages
Document CDN usage and caching infrastructure
Identify microservice architecture patterns from API responses

tests.name: Test Network Infrastructure Configuration
tests.description: Review the network infrastructure configuration for known vulnerabilities, unnecessary services, and default settings that could be exploited.
test_steps: Scan for open ports and running services on the target
Check for unnecessary services and default installations
Verify administrative interfaces are not publicly accessible
Test for known vulnerabilities in identified network services
Review firewall rules and network segmentation

tests.name: Test Application Platform Configuration
tests.description: Review the application platform configuration including web server, application server, and database server for security misconfigurations.
test_steps: Check for default credentials on application platforms
Verify unnecessary HTTP methods are disabled (TRACE, PUT, DELETE)
Check directory listing is disabled
Review server configuration for information leakage
Test for platform-specific vulnerabilities and misconfigurations

tests.name: Test File Extensions Handling for Sensitive Information
tests.description: Determine how the web server handles different file extensions and whether sensitive backup or configuration files can be accessed.
test_steps: Test for backup file extensions (.bak, .old, .orig, .copy, .tmp)
Request files with common source code extensions (.java, .py, .php~)
Check for configuration file extensions (.conf, .cfg, .ini, .xml)
Test for compressed archive files (.zip, .tar.gz, .rar)
Verify the server properly handles unknown file extensions

tests.name: Review Old Backup and Unreferenced Files for Sensitive Information
tests.description: Find and examine backup files, unreferenced files, and old versions that may contain sensitive information or source code.
test_steps: Brute-force common backup file names and paths
Check for version control metadata directories (.git, .svn, .hg)
Test for editor backup files (.swp, .swo, ~)
Look for database dump files and SQL backups
Search for log files accessible via the web server
Check for deployment artifacts and build files

tests.name: Enumerate Infrastructure and Application Admin Interfaces
tests.description: Identify administrative interfaces for the infrastructure and application that could provide elevated access if compromised.
test_steps: Brute-force common admin paths (/admin, /manager, /console, /phpmyadmin)
Check for admin interfaces on non-standard ports
Search for administrative interfaces referenced in robots.txt or sitemap
Test for default credentials on discovered admin panels
Verify admin interfaces require strong authentication

tests.name: Test HTTP Methods
tests.description: Enumerate the HTTP methods supported by the web server and application to identify potentially dangerous methods that could be exploited.
test_steps: Send OPTIONS request to enumerate supported methods
Test for TRACE method to check for cross-site tracing
Test PUT and DELETE methods for arbitrary file upload/deletion
Check for WebDAV methods (PROPFIND, MKCOL, COPY, MOVE)
Verify methods are consistently restricted across all endpoints

tests.name: Test HTTP Strict Transport Security
tests.description: Verify that the application properly implements HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) to prevent protocol downgrade attacks and cookie hijacking.
test_steps: Check for the Strict-Transport-Security response header
Verify HSTS max-age is sufficiently long (at least 31536000 seconds)
Check if includeSubDomains directive is present
Verify the preload directive is set if applicable
Test if the application redirects HTTP to HTTPS before setting HSTS

tests.name: Test RIA Cross Domain Policy
tests.description: Review Rich Internet Application cross-domain policy files to ensure they do not grant overly permissive access to external domains.
test_steps: Retrieve and analyze crossdomain.xml for Flash policies
Retrieve and analyze clientaccesspolicy.xml for Silverlight policies
Check for overly permissive allow-access-from domains (wildcard *)
Verify CORS headers are not overly permissive
Test if cross-domain policies expose sensitive endpoints

tests.name: Test File Permission
tests.description: Verify that file permissions on the web server are configured correctly to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive files and directories.
test_steps: Check for world-readable sensitive files (configuration, logs, databases)
Verify web server process runs with minimal privileges
Test for directory traversal to access files outside web root
Check upload directories for execute permissions
Verify temporary files are properly protected

tests.name: Test for Subdomain Takeover
tests.description: Identify subdomains that point to external services that are no longer active, which could allow an attacker to claim the subdomain.
test_steps: Enumerate all subdomains of the target domain
Check DNS CNAME records for subdomains pointing to external services
Verify if the external service endpoint is still claimed by the target
Test for dangling DNS records pointing to deprovisioned cloud resources
Check for expired or unclaimed third-party service registrations

tests.name: Test Cloud Storage
tests.description: Identify and test cloud storage resources (S3 buckets, Azure blobs, GCP buckets) associated with the target for misconfigurations and unauthorized access.
test_steps: Enumerate cloud storage bucket names associated with the target
Test for publicly listable bucket contents
Test for publicly readable objects in storage buckets
Test for publicly writable storage buckets
Check for sensitive data exposure in public cloud storage
Verify bucket policies and access control lists

tests.name: Test Role Definitions
tests.description: Verify that user roles are clearly defined with appropriate access permissions and that privilege escalation between roles is not possible.
test_steps: Enumerate all defined user roles in the application
Map permissions and accessible resources for each role
Verify role hierarchy is properly enforced
Test for horizontal privilege escalation between same-level roles
Check for undocumented or hidden roles with elevated privileges

tests.name: Test User Registration Process
tests.description: Analyze the user registration process for vulnerabilities including identity spoofing, duplicate registrations, and information disclosure.
test_steps: Test if registration can be completed with duplicate usernames or emails
Check for user enumeration via registration error messages
Verify email/identity verification is required before account activation
Test registration with malicious input (XSS, SQL injection payloads)
Check for rate limiting on the registration endpoint

tests.name: Test Account Provisioning Process
tests.description: Review the account provisioning and deprovisioning process to ensure accounts are created, modified, and deleted securely.
test_steps: Verify account provisioning requires proper authorization
Check if deprovisioned accounts are fully deactivated
Test for residual data after account deprovisioning
Verify provisioning process enforces required security controls
Check if accounts can be provisioned with elevated privileges without authorization

tests.name: Testing for Account Enumeration and Guessable User Account
tests.description: Determine whether it is possible to enumerate valid usernames or accounts through different application responses to valid and invalid credentials.
test_steps: Test login form responses for differences between valid and invalid usernames
Check password reset functionality for user enumeration
Analyze registration form for username existence disclosure
Compare HTTP response codes, timing, and content length for valid vs invalid users
Test for user enumeration via API endpoints
Check for predictable username patterns (admin, user1, user2)

tests.name: Testing for Weak or Unenforced Username Policy
tests.description: Assess the username policy to ensure it prevents creation of easily guessable or weak usernames and enforces proper naming conventions.
test_steps: Test registration with very short usernames (single character)
Test for usernames with special characters and encoding issues
Verify minimum username length requirements
Check if common default usernames are blocked (admin, test, root)
Test for case sensitivity issues in usernames

tests.name: Testing for Credentials Transported over an Encrypted Channel
tests.description: Verify that user credentials are always transmitted over an encrypted channel (HTTPS/TLS) and never sent in plaintext.
test_steps: Check if the login page is served over HTTPS
Verify the login form submits credentials over HTTPS
Test for HTTP to HTTPS redirect before credential submission
Check for mixed content on authentication pages
Verify API authentication endpoints enforce TLS

tests.name: Testing for Default Credentials
tests.description: Test for default credentials on the application, administrative interfaces, and supporting infrastructure components.
test_steps: Test common default username/password combinations on login forms
Check for default credentials on discovered admin interfaces
Test default credentials for identified frameworks and platforms
Verify database and infrastructure services are not using defaults
Check for hardcoded credentials in publicly accessible files

tests.name: Testing for Weak Lock Out Mechanism
tests.description: Evaluate the account lockout mechanism to determine if it effectively prevents brute-force attacks while avoiding denial of service to legitimate users.
test_steps: Attempt multiple failed logins to determine lockout threshold
Measure lockout duration and reset behavior
Test if lockout applies consistently across all authentication endpoints
Check if account lockout can be used for denial of service
Verify lockout notifications are sent to account owners
Test for CAPTCHA or progressive delays as alternative mechanisms

tests.name: Testing for Bypassing Authentication Schema
tests.description: Attempt to bypass the authentication mechanism by direct page requests, parameter modification, session ID prediction, or SQL injection.
test_steps: Attempt to access protected pages directly without authentication
Modify authentication parameters or tokens to bypass checks
Test for forced browsing to authenticated resources
Check for authentication bypass via parameter pollution
Test for SQL injection in authentication fields
Attempt to replay authentication tokens or session IDs

tests.name: Testing for Vulnerable Remember Password
tests.description: Analyze the remember password/remember me functionality for vulnerabilities that could allow credential theft or session hijacking.
test_steps: Check if remember-me tokens are stored securely in cookies
Verify remember-me tokens are not predictable or guessable
Test if remember-me functionality persists after password change
Check if credentials are stored in browser autocomplete-friendly fields
Verify remember-me tokens expire after a reasonable period

tests.name: Testing for Browser Cache Weaknesses
tests.description: Verify that the application properly instructs browsers not to cache sensitive authentication data including credentials and session tokens.
test_steps: Check Cache-Control and Pragma headers on authentication pages
Verify sensitive pages include no-store and no-cache directives
Test if credentials are cached in browser history after form submission
Check for autocomplete attributes on password fields
Verify back button does not reveal authenticated content after logout

tests.name: Testing for Weak Password Policy
tests.description: Evaluate the password policy to ensure it requires sufficiently complex passwords and prevents the use of common or easily guessable passwords.
test_steps: Test minimum and maximum password length requirements
Verify complexity requirements (uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters)
Test if common passwords from well-known wordlists are accepted
Check if password history is enforced to prevent reuse
Verify password policy is consistently enforced across all password change mechanisms

tests.name: Testing for Weak Security Question Answer
tests.description: Evaluate security questions used for account recovery or additional authentication for weaknesses that could allow an attacker to guess or research the answers.
test_steps: Review the security questions offered for guessability
Test if security question answers are case-sensitive
Check if answers can be brute-forced without lockout
Verify security questions cannot be changed without re-authentication
Test for self-chosen questions that may be trivially answerable

tests.name: Testing for Weak Password Change or Reset Functionality
tests.description: Evaluate password change and reset mechanisms for vulnerabilities including token predictability, lack of expiration, and missing old password verification.
test_steps: Test if password change requires the current password
Verify password reset tokens are random and unpredictable
Check if password reset tokens expire within a reasonable time
Test for user enumeration through the password reset process
Verify password reset invalidates existing sessions
Test if reset links can be reused after password change

tests.name: Testing for Weaker Authentication in Alternative Channel
tests.description: Identify alternative authentication channels (mobile app, API, call center) and verify they enforce the same security controls as the primary channel.
test_steps: Identify all authentication channels (web, mobile, API, legacy endpoints)
Compare authentication strength across all channels
Test for weaker lockout policies on alternative channels
Check if alternative channels support MFA consistently
Verify password policies are enforced across all channels

tests.name: Testing Directory Traversal File Include
tests.description: Test for directory traversal and file inclusion vulnerabilities that could allow unauthorized access to files and directories outside the web root.
test_steps: Test URL parameters with directory traversal sequences (../, ..\)
Attempt to read sensitive system files (/etc/passwd, win.ini)
Test for local file inclusion (LFI) in include/template parameters
Test for remote file inclusion (RFI) with external URLs
Use encoding techniques to bypass traversal filters (URL encoding, double encoding, null bytes)
Test file path parameters in API endpoints

tests.name: Testing for Bypassing Authorization Schema
tests.description: Test whether authorization controls can be bypassed to access resources or functionality belonging to other users or higher privilege levels.
test_steps: Access resources belonging to other users by changing identifiers (IDOR)
Test horizontal privilege escalation by switching user context
Test vertical privilege escalation by accessing admin functions as regular user
Attempt to access API endpoints without proper authorization tokens
Test for missing function-level access control on sensitive operations
Modify role or group parameters in requests to elevate privileges

tests.name: Testing for Privilege Escalation
tests.description: Test whether an authenticated user can escalate their privileges to gain unauthorized access to higher-level functions or other users' data.
test_steps: Map accessible functionality for each user role
Attempt to access higher-privileged functions with lower-privileged accounts
Test for IDOR in resource identifiers (user IDs, document IDs)
Modify user role parameters in requests (role=admin, isAdmin=true)
Test API endpoints for missing authorization checks on state-changing operations

tests.name: Testing for Insecure Direct Object References
tests.description: Test for insecure direct object references (IDOR) where user-supplied input is used to directly access objects without proper authorization checks.
test_steps: Identify parameters referencing internal objects (IDs, filenames, keys)
Modify object reference parameters to access other users' resources
Test with sequential IDs, UUIDs, and encoded references
Check for authorization bypass in file download and API endpoints
Test mass assignment vulnerabilities in object update operations

tests.name: Testing for Session Management Schema
tests.description: Analyze the session management implementation to ensure session tokens are generated, transmitted, and stored securely throughout their lifecycle.
test_steps: Analyze session token format, length, and randomness
Check if session tokens are transmitted via secure cookies
Verify session cookies have Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite flags
Test session token entropy and predictability
Verify session tokens are not exposed in URLs or logs

tests.name: Testing for Cookies Attributes
tests.description: Verify that session cookies are configured with proper security attributes to prevent interception, theft, and unauthorized access.
test_steps: Check for Secure flag on all session cookies
Check for HttpOnly flag to prevent JavaScript access
Verify SameSite attribute is set to Strict or Lax
Check cookie Domain and Path scope for over-broad settings
Verify cookie expiration is appropriately configured
Test for sensitive data stored in cookies

tests.name: Testing for Session Fixation
tests.description: Test whether the application is vulnerable to session fixation attacks where an attacker can force a known session ID onto a user.
test_steps: Obtain a session token before authentication
Authenticate and check if the session token changes
Test if a pre-set session token is accepted by the application
Check if session tokens can be set via URL parameters
Verify the application generates a new session after login

tests.name: Testing for Exposed Session Variables
tests.description: Determine if session tokens or sensitive session data are exposed through URLs, logs, error messages, or other client-accessible mechanisms.
test_steps: Check if session IDs appear in URLs or query strings
Verify session tokens are not logged in access logs
Test for session token exposure in Referer headers
Check if session data is exposed in client-side storage (localStorage, sessionStorage)
Verify sensitive session variables are not cached by browsers or proxies

tests.name: Testing for Cross Site Request Forgery
tests.description: Test whether the application is vulnerable to CSRF attacks that could allow an attacker to perform unauthorized actions on behalf of authenticated users.
test_steps: Identify state-changing operations (form submissions, API calls)
Check for anti-CSRF tokens in forms and AJAX requests
Test if anti-CSRF tokens are properly validated server-side
Check for SameSite cookie attribute as CSRF mitigation
Attempt to forge requests to state-changing endpoints without valid CSRF tokens
Test if CSRF tokens are tied to the user session

tests.name: Testing for Logout Functionality
tests.description: Verify that the logout function properly terminates the user session and invalidates all associated tokens both client-side and server-side.
test_steps: Capture session token before logout
Perform logout and verify session cookie is cleared
Attempt to access protected resources using the captured session token
Verify server-side session is invalidated on logout
Check for single sign-out in SSO environments

tests.name: Testing Session Timeout
tests.description: Verify that sessions expire after an appropriate period of inactivity to minimize the window for session hijacking.
test_steps: Determine the session idle timeout by waiting and re-accessing protected resources
Verify absolute session timeout is configured regardless of activity
Test if session timeout is enforced server-side, not just client-side
Check if concurrent sessions are limited per user
Verify expired sessions cannot be reused

tests.name: Testing for Session Puzzling
tests.description: Test for session variable overloading where the same session variable is used for different purposes across multiple application flows, potentially leading to authentication bypass.
test_steps: Map all application flows that modify session variables
Identify session variables shared between different flows
Test if accessing one flow affects the session state of another
Attempt to bypass authentication by manipulating shared session variables
Check for race conditions in session variable updates

tests.name: Testing for Session Hijacking
tests.description: Test the application's resistance to session hijacking attacks where an attacker takes over a legitimate user's session through token theft or prediction.
test_steps: Analyze session token randomness and unpredictability
Test for session token prediction by collecting and analyzing multiple tokens
Check if session tokens are transmitted only over encrypted channels
Verify session is bound to client characteristics (IP, User-Agent)
Test for session token theft via XSS, network sniffing, or log exposure

tests.name: Testing for Reflected Cross Site Scripting
tests.description: Test for reflected XSS vulnerabilities where user-supplied input is immediately returned in the server response without proper sanitization.
test_steps: Identify all parameters reflected in application responses
Inject basic XSS payloads (<script>alert(1)</script>) in reflected parameters
Test with encoding variations to bypass input filters
Test XSS in HTTP headers reflected in responses
Verify both GET and POST parameters for reflected XSS
Test for DOM-based reflection through server responses

tests.name: Testing for Stored Cross Site Scripting
tests.description: Test for stored XSS vulnerabilities where malicious input is permanently stored on the server and served to other users viewing the affected content.
test_steps: Identify all input fields that store data (comments, profiles, messages)
Inject XSS payloads into stored data fields
Verify if payloads execute when content is viewed by other users
Test rich text editors and file upload names for stored XSS
Check for XSS in administrative views of user-submitted data
Test SVG and HTML file uploads for stored XSS

tests.name: Testing for HTTP Verb Tampering
tests.description: Test whether the application properly validates HTTP methods and whether security controls can be bypassed by using unexpected HTTP verbs.
test_steps: Test accessing protected resources with different HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, HEAD)
Send requests with arbitrary HTTP verbs to bypass security filters
Test if method override headers (X-HTTP-Method-Override) bypass controls
Verify authorization checks are method-agnostic
Check for REST API method confusion (GET vs POST for state changes)

tests.name: Testing for HTTP Parameter Pollution
tests.description: Test for HTTP parameter pollution vulnerabilities where duplicate parameters are handled inconsistently to bypass security controls or alter application logic.
test_steps: Send requests with duplicate parameters containing different values
Test parameter pollution across different HTTP methods
Check if WAF/security filters can be bypassed via parameter pollution
Test for server-side parameter precedence issues
Verify parameter handling consistency between frontend and backend

tests.name: Testing for SQL Injection
tests.description: Test for SQL injection vulnerabilities that could allow an attacker to interact with the application's database, potentially reading, modifying, or deleting data.
test_steps: Identify all input parameters that may interact with databases
Test for error-based SQL injection using single quotes and syntax errors
Test for blind SQL injection using boolean-based and time-based techniques
Test UNION-based SQL injection to extract data from other tables
Test for second-order SQL injection in stored data
Use automated tools to comprehensively test all injection points

tests.name: Testing for LDAP Injection
tests.description: Test for LDAP injection vulnerabilities in applications that construct LDAP queries using user-supplied input.
test_steps: Identify input fields that may interact with LDAP directories
Inject LDAP metacharacters (*, (, ), \, NUL) into input fields
Test for LDAP injection in authentication mechanisms
Attempt to modify LDAP queries to bypass access controls
Test for information disclosure through LDAP error messages

tests.name: Testing for XML Injection
tests.description: Test for XML injection vulnerabilities where user input is incorporated into XML documents without proper sanitization, potentially altering document structure.
test_steps: Identify endpoints that accept XML input
Inject XML metacharacters to alter document structure
Test for XML external entity (XXE) injection
Test for XML entity expansion (billion laughs) denial of service
Check for XPath injection in XML processing
Test SOAP endpoints for XML injection

tests.name: Testing for SSI Injection
tests.description: Test for Server-Side Include (SSI) injection vulnerabilities where user input is processed by SSI directives on the web server.
test_steps: Identify if the web server supports SSI processing
Inject SSI directives (<!--#exec cmd="id"--> ) in input fields
Test for SSI injection in file upload functionality
Check for SSI processing in user-controlled content areas
Test for command execution through SSI directives

tests.name: Testing for XPath Injection
tests.description: Test for XPath injection vulnerabilities in applications that use XPath queries to navigate XML documents based on user-supplied input.
test_steps: Identify input fields used in XML/XPath-based queries
Inject XPath syntax characters (' , ") to trigger errors
Test for authentication bypass using XPath injection (string='or '1'='1)
Attempt to extract XML document contents via XPath injection
Test for blind XPath injection using boolean conditions

tests.name: Testing for IMAP SMTP Injection
tests.description: Test for email header injection and IMAP/SMTP command injection in application features that interact with mail servers.
test_steps: Identify functionality that sends or processes emails (contact forms, registration)
Inject SMTP header separators (\r\n) in email-related fields
Test for additional recipient injection (CC, BCC)
Test IMAP command injection in webmail-type applications
Check for email content injection and mail relay abuse

tests.name: Testing for Code Injection
tests.description: Test for server-side code injection vulnerabilities where user input is evaluated as code by the application runtime.
test_steps: Identify parameters that may be passed to eval() or similar functions
Inject language-specific code payloads (PHP, Python, Node.js, Ruby)
Test for template injection in server-side template engines
Check for code execution through deserialization of user input
Test file upload functionality for executable code injection
Verify input validation prevents code execution patterns

tests.name: Testing for Command Injection
tests.description: Test for OS command injection vulnerabilities where user input is passed to system shell commands without proper sanitization.
test_steps: Identify parameters passed to system commands (ping, traceroute, file ops)
Inject command separators (; | & || && \n) with additional commands
Test for blind command injection using time delays (sleep, ping -c)
Test for out-of-band command injection (DNS, HTTP callbacks)
Test with encoding and escaping to bypass input filters
Verify command injection in file upload filenames and paths

tests.name: Testing for Format String Injection
tests.description: Test for format string vulnerabilities where user-supplied input is used as a format string parameter in functions like printf().
test_steps: Identify input fields that may be processed by format string functions
Inject format string specifiers (%s, %x, %n, %p) in input fields
Monitor application responses for memory disclosure or crashes
Test for format string injection in logging mechanisms
Verify the application does not pass user input as format strings

tests.name: Testing for Incubated Vulnerability
tests.description: Test for incubated (second-order) vulnerabilities where malicious input is stored and later executed in a different context or by a different function.
test_steps: Identify stored input that is used in different application contexts
Inject payloads in registration/profile data that may be processed later
Test for second-order SQL injection through stored data
Check for stored XSS that triggers in admin or reporting interfaces
Test file uploads that are processed asynchronously by backend services

tests.name: Testing for HTTP Splitting Smuggling
tests.description: Test for HTTP request splitting and smuggling vulnerabilities that exploit differences in how frontend and backend servers parse HTTP requests.
test_steps: Test for HTTP response splitting by injecting CRLF in headers
Test for HTTP request smuggling using CL.TE and TE.CL techniques
Inject CRLF sequences in input parameters reflected in headers
Test for header injection in redirect URLs and cookie values
Check for differences in Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding handling

tests.name: Testing for HTTP Incoming Requests
tests.description: Test how the application handles unexpected or malformed incoming HTTP requests, including oversized headers, malformed URLs, and protocol violations.
test_steps: Send requests with extremely long URLs and headers
Test with malformed HTTP request syntax
Send requests with unexpected Content-Type headers
Test for request smuggling via malformed chunk encoding
Verify the application handles edge cases in HTTP parsing securely

tests.name: Testing for Host Header Injection
tests.description: Test for host header injection vulnerabilities where the Host header is used in application logic such as password reset links, redirects, or cache keys.
test_steps: Modify the Host header and observe application behavior
Test for password reset poisoning via manipulated Host header
Check for cache poisoning using different Host header values
Test X-Forwarded-Host and X-Host header injection
Verify the application validates the Host header against an allowlist
Test for SSRF via Host header manipulation

tests.name: Testing for Server-Side Template Injection
tests.description: Test for server-side template injection (SSTI) vulnerabilities where user input is embedded into server-side templates, potentially leading to remote code execution.
test_steps: Identify input reflected in template-rendered output
Inject template syntax for common engines ({{7*7}}, ${7*7}, <%= 7*7 %>)
Determine the template engine from successful math execution
Escalate from template injection to code execution
Test for sandbox escape in template engines with restricted contexts
Check error messages for template engine identification

tests.name: Testing for Server-Side Request Forgery
tests.description: Test for server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerabilities where the application can be tricked into making requests to unintended internal or external resources.
test_steps: Identify parameters that accept URLs or hostnames as input
Test for SSRF by requesting internal resources (127.0.0.1, localhost, internal IPs)
Attempt to access cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254)
Test SSRF with various URL schemes (file://, gopher://, dict://)
Check for blind SSRF using out-of-band detection (DNS, HTTP callbacks)
Test bypasses for SSRF filters (IP encoding, DNS rebinding, redirects)

tests.name: Testing for Improper Error Handling
tests.description: Test for improper error handling that reveals sensitive information such as stack traces, database details, internal paths, or software versions.
test_steps: Trigger application errors with invalid input and observe error responses
Request non-existent pages and resources to check custom error pages
Submit unexpected data types and malformed requests
Check for stack traces, SQL errors, and debug information in responses
Test different request methods on endpoints to trigger errors
Verify error messages do not disclose internal architecture details

tests.name: Testing for Stack Traces
tests.description: Verify that the application does not expose stack traces or detailed debug information to users, which could reveal sensitive internal implementation details.
test_steps: Trigger exceptions through various injection techniques
Send malformed JSON/XML payloads to trigger parsing errors
Test API endpoints with unexpected data types and missing parameters
Check for verbose error modes enabled in production (DEBUG=True)
Verify custom error handlers mask internal details

tests.name: Testing for Weak Transport Layer Security
tests.description: Assess the TLS/SSL configuration of the server to identify weak protocols, cipher suites, and certificate issues that could compromise transport security.
test_steps: Test for support of deprecated protocols (SSLv2, SSLv3, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1)
Enumerate supported cipher suites and identify weak ones
Check for certificate validity, chain, and trust issues
Test for known TLS vulnerabilities (BEAST, CRIME, POODLE, Heartbleed, DROWN)
Verify HSTS and certificate pinning implementation
Check for proper certificate hostname matching

tests.name: Testing for Padding Oracle
tests.description: Test for padding oracle vulnerabilities in applications using block cipher encryption with padding, which could allow decryption of encrypted data.
test_steps: Identify encrypted values in cookies, parameters, and tokens
Modify ciphertext bytes and observe application error responses
Look for differences in error responses indicating padding validity
Test for padding oracle in viewstate, authentication tokens, and session data
Use automated tools to exploit confirmed padding oracle vulnerabilities

tests.name: Testing for Sensitive Information Sent via Unencrypted Channels
tests.description: Verify that all sensitive data (credentials, personal information, tokens) is transmitted exclusively over encrypted channels.
test_steps: Check if any application pages transmit data over HTTP instead of HTTPS
Verify login forms and authentication APIs use HTTPS exclusively
Test for mixed content where secure pages load resources over HTTP
Check for sensitive data in URL query parameters visible in logs
Verify API communications enforce TLS for all data exchanges

tests.name: Testing for Weak Encryption
tests.description: Identify the use of weak or obsolete cryptographic algorithms and implementations that could be exploited to compromise data confidentiality or integrity.
test_steps: Identify cryptographic algorithms used by the application
Check for weak algorithms (MD5, SHA1, DES, RC4, ECB mode)
Test for insufficient key lengths in encryption implementations
Verify random number generation uses cryptographically secure sources
Check for custom or home-grown cryptographic implementations
Test for cryptographic key exposure in client-side code or configuration

tests.name: Test Business Logic Data Validation
tests.description: Verify that the application properly validates business logic data to prevent processing of invalid, unexpected, or manipulated data values.
test_steps: Identify business rules governing data input (price ranges, quantities, dates)
Submit boundary values and out-of-range data for business fields
Test negative values where only positive are expected (negative prices, quantities)
Submit data in unexpected formats or types for business-critical fields
Test for logic bypass by manipulating hidden or calculated fields

tests.name: Test Ability to Forge Requests
tests.description: Test whether an attacker can forge or manipulate requests to bypass intended business logic flows and achieve unauthorized outcomes.
test_steps: Identify multi-step business processes and their expected sequence
Attempt to skip intermediate steps in multi-step workflows
Replay and modify captured legitimate requests
Test for timestamp and sequence manipulation in business transactions
Verify server-side validation of all business-critical parameters

tests.name: Test Integrity Checks
tests.description: Verify that the application enforces integrity checks to prevent unauthorized modification of data during transmission and processing.
test_steps: Modify hidden form fields and verify server-side validation
Tamper with pricing and quantity data in purchase workflows
Test for client-side-only validation of critical business data
Modify API request bodies between steps in multi-step processes
Check for HMAC or signature validation on sensitive parameters

tests.name: Test for Process Timing
tests.description: Test whether business processes can be exploited through timing manipulation, including race conditions and time-of-check/time-of-use vulnerabilities.
test_steps: Identify time-sensitive operations (promotions, auctions, one-time-use codes)
Test race conditions by sending concurrent identical requests
Exploit TOCTOU vulnerabilities in balance checks and resource allocation
Test for double-spending in payment and point redemption systems
Verify atomic operations for critical business transactions

tests.name: Test Number of Times a Function Can Be Used Limits
tests.description: Verify that business functions with intended usage limits are properly enforced and cannot be used more than the allowed number of times.
test_steps: Identify functions with usage limits (discount codes, free trials, votes)
Attempt to use limited functions beyond their allowed count
Test for rate limit bypass through parameter manipulation
Check if limits are enforced per session, per user, or per IP
Test for limit reset by creating new accounts or sessions

tests.name: Testing for the Circumvention of Work Flows
tests.description: Test whether the application's intended workflow sequence can be circumvented to reach unintended states or bypass required steps.
test_steps: Map the complete workflow with all required steps
Attempt to access later steps directly without completing earlier ones
Test for workflow bypass by modifying step-tracking parameters
Skip payment or verification steps in purchase workflows
Test if completed workflow steps can be revisited and modified

tests.name: Test Defenses Against Application Misuse
tests.description: Verify the application has adequate defenses against misuse such as automation, scraping, and abuse of legitimate functionality.
test_steps: Test for rate limiting on sensitive operations
Verify CAPTCHA or other anti-automation mechanisms are in place
Test for account lockout after excessive failed operations
Check for monitoring and alerting on suspicious usage patterns
Test if anti-abuse mechanisms can be bypassed

tests.name: Test Upload of Unexpected File Types
tests.description: Test whether the application properly restricts file uploads to only expected types and prevents upload of potentially malicious files.
test_steps: Identify all file upload functionality in the application
Attempt to upload files with dangerous extensions (.php, .asp, .jsp, .exe)
Test content-type manipulation to bypass upload restrictions
Upload files with double extensions (file.php.jpg) and null bytes
Verify server-side validation of file content, not just extension
Test for upload of oversized files and zip bombs

tests.name: Test Upload of Malicious Files
tests.description: Test whether uploaded files are properly scanned and sandboxed to prevent execution of malicious payloads on the server or against other users.
test_steps: Upload web shells in various formats (PHP, ASP, JSP)
Test for execution of uploaded files by accessing them directly
Upload files containing XSS payloads (SVG, HTML, XML)
Test for path traversal in upload filename handling
Verify uploaded files are stored outside the web root
Check if uploaded files retain their original dangerous content type

tests.name: Testing for DOM-Based Cross Site Scripting
tests.description: Test for DOM-based XSS vulnerabilities where the attack payload is executed as a result of modifying the DOM environment in the victim's browser.
test_steps: Identify DOM sinks (innerHTML, document.write, eval, location) in JavaScript
Trace data flow from DOM sources (location.hash, document.referrer) to sinks
Inject XSS payloads via URL fragments and DOM-accessible inputs
Test for DOM XSS in client-side JavaScript frameworks
Verify client-side input sanitization of DOM-sourced data
Check for postMessage handlers that process untrusted data

tests.name: Testing for JavaScript Execution
tests.description: Test for JavaScript execution vulnerabilities where user-controlled data is passed to JavaScript execution functions without proper sanitization.
test_steps: Identify code using eval(), setTimeout(), setInterval() with user data
Test for script injection in dynamically created script elements
Check for JavaScript execution via protocol handlers (javascript:)
Test event handler attributes for injection (onclick, onerror)
Verify Content Security Policy headers restrict inline script execution

tests.name: Testing for HTML Injection
tests.description: Test for HTML injection vulnerabilities where user input is embedded into the HTML response without proper encoding, allowing injection of arbitrary HTML elements.
test_steps: Identify input parameters reflected in HTML responses
Inject HTML tags and verify they render in the page
Test for HTML injection in error messages and user-generated content
Check for phishing attacks through injected HTML forms
Verify HTML encoding is applied to all user-controlled output contexts

tests.name: Testing for Client-side URL Redirect
tests.description: Test for open redirect vulnerabilities where user-controlled input is used in client-side URL redirections without proper validation.
test_steps: Identify parameters used in client-side redirects (window.location, meta refresh)
Test redirect parameters with external domain URLs
Test for redirect bypass techniques (//evil.com, /\evil.com)
Check for JavaScript protocol in redirect parameters
Verify redirect URL validation uses an allowlist approach

tests.name: Testing for CSS Injection
tests.description: Test for CSS injection vulnerabilities where user input is incorporated into CSS styles, potentially leading to data exfiltration or UI manipulation.
test_steps: Identify user input reflected in CSS contexts (style attributes, stylesheets)
Inject CSS to modify page appearance and create phishing overlays
Test for data exfiltration using CSS selectors and background-image URLs
Check for CSS expression() execution in older browsers
Verify CSS input sanitization prevents malicious style injection

tests.name: Testing for Client-side Resource Manipulation
tests.description: Test for vulnerabilities where user-controlled input can manipulate resources loaded by the client, such as script sources, image URLs, or iframe targets.
test_steps: Identify user input used in resource URLs (src, href, action attributes)
Test for JavaScript source manipulation to load malicious scripts
Check for iframe source manipulation for clickjacking or phishing
Test for link injection in dynamically generated resource references
Verify resource URLs are validated against an allowlist

tests.name: Testing Cross Origin Resource Sharing
tests.description: Test CORS configuration for overly permissive settings that could allow unauthorized cross-origin access to sensitive application data.
test_steps: Check Access-Control-Allow-Origin header for wildcard or reflective values
Test if arbitrary origins are reflected in CORS response headers
Verify Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is not used with wildcard origin
Test for CORS misconfiguration on sensitive API endpoints
Check if null origin is allowed in CORS policy
Verify pre-flight requests are properly validated

tests.name: Testing for Cross Site Flashing
tests.description: Test Flash cross-domain policies and Flash-based functionality for vulnerabilities that could allow cross-site data access or code execution.
test_steps: Identify Flash content and SWF files served by the application
Review crossdomain.xml for overly permissive policies
Test for FlashVars manipulation for XSS or data injection
Check for insecure ExternalInterface calls in Flash objects
Verify Flash content does not expose sensitive functionality

tests.name: Testing for Clickjacking
tests.description: Test whether the application is vulnerable to clickjacking attacks where transparent overlays trick users into clicking on hidden elements.
test_steps: Check for X-Frame-Options header (DENY or SAMEORIGIN)
Verify Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive
Attempt to embed the application in an iframe on an external page
Test for frame-busting JavaScript and its bypass potential
Check critical functionality pages for framing protection
Test for partial clickjacking on specific UI elements

tests.name: Testing WebSockets
tests.description: Test WebSocket implementations for security vulnerabilities including authentication, authorization, input validation, and cross-site WebSocket hijacking.
test_steps: Identify WebSocket endpoints and their connection handshake
Test for cross-site WebSocket hijacking (CSWSH) via Origin validation
Check for authentication and authorization in WebSocket connections
Test for injection vulnerabilities in WebSocket messages
Verify WebSocket connections use secure transport (wss://)
Test for denial of service through message flooding

tests.name: Testing Web Messaging
tests.description: Test HTML5 Web Messaging (postMessage) implementations for vulnerabilities in origin validation and message handling that could lead to XSS or data theft.
test_steps: Identify postMessage senders and receivers in JavaScript code
Check if message receivers validate the origin of incoming messages
Test for XSS through postMessage data passed to dangerous sinks
Verify sensitive data is not sent via postMessage to untrusted origins
Test for message handler confusion between different message types

tests.name: Testing Browser Storage
tests.description: Test client-side storage mechanisms (localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies) for sensitive data exposure and injection vulnerabilities.
test_steps: Enumerate data stored in localStorage and sessionStorage
Check for sensitive data (tokens, PII, credentials) in browser storage
Verify stored data is properly cleared on logout
Test for injection through data loaded from browser storage
Check for cross-origin access to stored data
Verify IndexedDB databases do not contain sensitive information

tests.name: Testing for Cross Site Script Inclusion
tests.description: Test for cross-site script inclusion (XSSI) vulnerabilities where sensitive data in JavaScript files can be stolen by including them from an attacker-controlled page.
test_steps: Identify dynamic JavaScript files that contain user-specific data
Test if sensitive JavaScript endpoints can be included cross-origin
Check for JSONP endpoints that return sensitive data without token validation
Verify authentication is required for JavaScript files containing sensitive data
Test for data leakage through JavaScript variable overriding

tests.name: Testing GraphQL
tests.description: Test GraphQL API implementations for security vulnerabilities including introspection exposure, injection, authorization bypass, and denial of service.
test_steps: Test for introspection query exposure to enumerate the full schema
Check for authorization bypass in GraphQL resolvers
Test for injection vulnerabilities in GraphQL query parameters
Test for denial of service through deeply nested or complex queries
Verify query depth and complexity limits are enforced
Check for sensitive data exposure in GraphQL error messages

tests.name: Testing REST API
tests.description: Test REST API implementations for security vulnerabilities including authentication weaknesses, broken access control, injection, and improper data exposure.
test_steps: Enumerate API endpoints and HTTP methods through documentation and fuzzing
Test authentication mechanisms (API keys, OAuth, JWT) for weaknesses
Test for IDOR and broken access control across API endpoints
Check for mass assignment vulnerabilities in object creation/update
Test for injection vulnerabilities in API parameters and headers
Verify rate limiting and throttling on API endpoints

tests.name: Testing SOAP API
tests.description: Test SOAP API implementations for security vulnerabilities including XML-based attacks, WSDL exposure, and improper input validation.
test_steps: Retrieve and analyze WSDL file for exposed operations and data types
Test for XML external entity (XXE) injection in SOAP requests
Test for SQL injection in SOAP message parameters
Check for SOAP action spoofing attacks
Test for XML bomb and entity expansion denial of service
Verify WS-Security implementation for authentication and message integrity
